papers.title: Gut‒liver‒brain axis signature of cirrhosis-related cognitive impairment is consistent across multi-national cohorts.
papers.abstract: Cognitive impairment in cirrhosis is associated with an altered gut‒liver‒brain axis, but geographic variations in diet and clinical practices may limit generalizability. We investigated consistency of microbial signatures for cirrhosis-related cognitive impairment across four countries. We enrolled outpatients with cirrhosis from USA, Denmark, Lithuania, and Mexico who underwent Psychometric Hepatic Encephalopathy Score (PHES) testing for covert hepatic encephalopathy (CHE), and stool shotgun metagenomic sequencing. Taxonomic and functional associations with PHES were evaluated after adjustme
papers.summary: This study examined whether gut microbiome signatures associated with cognitive impairment in cirrhosis are consistent across patients from four countries (USA, Denmark, Lithuania, Mexico). Using stool shotgun metagenomics and PHES testing for covert hepatic encephalopathy, the authors identified taxonomic and functional microbial associations with cognitive scores that held across diverse dietary and clinical settings. The findings suggest a generalizable gut‒liver‒brain axis signature for cirrhosis-related cognitive impairment.

papers.title: Multi-scale hybrid correction of noisy long reads.
papers.abstract: Long-read sequencing offers superior genome resolution but is hindered by error rates of 1-15%. Existing correction methods often struggle to suppress sequencing errors without removing genuine biological variation, leading to over-correction. DADEC addresses this trade-off through a confidence-ordered framework comprising stringent de Bruijn graph (DBG) correction, haplotype-aware short-read alignment refinement, and permissive DBG recovery. Across seven simulated and three real datasets, DADEC achieved the lowest mismatch and indel rates in most benchmark settings while maintaining high hapl
papers.summary: DADEC is a new hybrid error-correction pipeline for noisy long reads that combines stringent de Bruijn graph correction, haplotype-aware short-read alignment refinement, and permissive de Bruijn graph recovery in a confidence-ordered framework. Across seven simulated and three real datasets, it achieved the lowest mismatch and indel rates in most benchmarks while preserving genuine biological variation, avoiding the over-correction that plagues existing methods.

papers.title: A specialized microbiome enriched in nitrification and halogen cycling potential resolved from multi-omics investigation of a Caribbean suboxic and acidic marine sinkhole.
papers.abstract: The Luymes Sinkholes, located on the Luymes Bank northwest of Saba, represent a unique marine environment characterized by distinct biogeochemical gradients. Most noticeable is an acidic (pH ≈ 6.25) and suboxic (O2 < 60 µmol/kg) submerged 'lake' at ~ 220 m depth exhibiting extreme deviations from standard oceanographic patterns, including elevated inorganic carbon, nitrate, and phosphate, and a lower temperature (20.3 ºC vs 26.4 ºC). To determine how the microbiome within the submerged acid lake adapted to these unique conditions, we collected 59 coupled samples of size-filtered (0.22 µm) plan
papers.summary: This study characterizes the microbiome of a unique Caribbean marine sinkhole containing an acidic (pH ~6.25) and suboxic submerged lake at ~220 m depth, using multi-omics approaches on 59 size-filtered samples. The researchers resolved a specialized microbial community enriched in nitrification and halogen cycling potential, demonstrating how microbes adapt to extreme biogeochemical gradients that deviate strongly from standard oceanographic conditions.

papers.title: Aerobic methane oxidation by microorganisms exacerbates neurotoxic methylmercury accumulation in rice paddy fields.
papers.abstract: Aerobic methane (CH4) oxidation is the dominant biological sink for CH4 in wetland soils and is increasingly linked to diverse biogeochemical processes; however, whether and how aerobic CH4 oxidation influences the production of the neurotoxin methylmercury (MeHg) through microbial mercury (Hg) methylation remains poorly understood. Here, we combined a ~3300 km field survey across the main rice-producing areas of China with 13CH4-DNA-stable isotope probing (SIP) to investigate the microbial linkage between aerobic CH4 oxidation and Hg methylation in paddy fields. Field observations showed posi
papers.summary: A large-scale field survey across China's rice-growing regions, combined with 13CH4-DNA stable isotope probing, reveals a positive association between aerobic methane oxidation and microbial mercury methylation in paddy soils. The findings suggest that microbes oxidizing methane also contribute to producing neurotoxic methylmercury, which then accumulates in rice, linking methane cycling to a major food-safety hazard.

papers.title: Patterns and determinants of antibiotic exposure during the first 2 years of life: a prospective birth cohort study in Switzerland.
papers.summary: This prospective birth cohort study in Switzerland characterized patterns and determinants of antibiotic exposure during the first 2 years of life. It found that antibiotic use was common and varied by factors such as parental characteristics, childcare attendance, and season, providing insights for antimicrobial stewardship in early childhood.

papers.title: Infant RSV immunity study (IRIS): protocol for a prospective birth cohort in Vancouver, Canada examining how age at respiratory syncytial virus exposure affects how infants respond to the virus immunologically.
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of severe respiratory illness in infants. Age at first infection is strongly associated with disease severity. Infants exposed to RSV at a younger age may not produce an immune response against RSV that is as protective as infection at a later age, and early life infection may influence the risk of recurrent or persistent wheezing, or subsequent asthma. However, how immune development at the time of exposure shapes RSV-specific immunity and long-term respiratory health remains unclear.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a prospective birth cohort in Vancouver, Canada, designed to track infants from birth to determine how the age at first RSV exposure shapes their immune response and long-term respiratory health. The study aims to clarify whether early-life RSV infection produces weaker protective immunity and increases risk of recurrent wheezing or asthma. As a protocol paper, it outlines the study design rather than reporting findings.

papers.title: Draft genome sequences of Desulfobulbus oralis strains reconstructed from archeological dental calculus of ancient Pacific Islanders.
papers.abstract: We present draft metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) of Desulfobulbus oralis strains reconstructed from ancient Pacific Islander dental calculus. MAGs were reconstructed via reference-guided read recruitment, de novo assembly, and metagenomic binning, displaying average nucleotide identities ≥96.4% to the D. oralis ATCC HOT041 reference genome, with completeness ≥50% and contamination ≤2.38%.
papers.summary: Researchers reconstructed draft metagenome-assembled genomes of Desulfobulbus oralis, an oral bacterium, from ancient dental calculus of Pacific Islanders. The genomes show high similarity (≥96.4% ANI) to a modern reference strain but are only moderately complete (≥50%), providing a glimpse into the oral microbiome of past populations.

papers.title: PEONY: a global reference database of DNA viral (vOTU) sequences from viral size-fractionated metagenomes (viromes).
papers.abstract: We present an update to the Phages and Integrated Genomes Encapsidated or Not reference database of DNA viral sequences (viral operational taxonomic units [vOTUs], mostly dsDNA bacteriophages) from global ecosystems. To reflect the inclusion of only virus size-fractionated metagenome- (virome-)derived vOTUs, we reintroduce the database as Phages Encapsidated ONlY.
papers.summary: PEONY is an updated global reference database of DNA viral sequences (vOTUs, mostly dsDNA bacteriophages) derived exclusively from virus size-fractionated metagenomes (viromes). The update rebrands the previous database to reflect that it now contains only encapsidated viral sequences from viromes across global ecosystems, providing a cleaner reference for viral ecology and metagenomic studies.

papers.title: An antibiotic-treated mouse model reveals the progression of intestinal botulism.
papers.abstract: Intestinal botulism, including infant botulism and adult intestinal toxemia botulism, is a life-threatening disease caused by intestinal infection with Clostridium botulinum (Cb) spores. Infants are particularly susceptible to Cb infection because of their immature gut microbiota, whereas healthy adults are generally protected by gut microbiota-mediated colonization resistance. Thus, immature gut microbiota or gut dysbiosis is thought to permit Cb colonization. However, the mechanisms underlying colonization resistance and disease progression remain poorly characterized. Here, using adult mice
papers.summary: This study establishes an antibiotic-treated adult mouse model of intestinal botulism, showing that disrupting the gut microbiota allows Clostridium botulinum spores to colonize the intestine and cause disease. The model provides a tractable system to study how gut microbiota-mediated colonization resistance normally prevents Cb infection and how dysbiosis permits disease progression.

papers.title: Temperature effects on life history strategies for rapid growth potential of leaf epiphytic bacteria.
papers.abstract: Phyllosphere bacteria, occupying both epiphytic and endophytic habitats, constitute a critical plant-atmosphere interface. However, their community assembly and life-history strategies (LHSs) in response to temperature increase remain poorly understood. Here, we compared leaf phyllosphere bacterial communities with those in other plant compartments across four representative plant species from an alpine meadow on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. By combining observations along an elevational gradient with a controlled warming experiment, we found that temperature was closely associated with the dete
papers.summary: This study examined how temperature shapes the life-history strategies of leaf-dwelling (phyllosphere) bacteria across four alpine meadow plant species on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, combining an elevational gradient survey with a controlled warming experiment. The authors found that temperature is closely tied to the composition and assembly of epiphytic versus endophytic bacterial communities, with warming favoring rapid-growth life-history strategies. The work highlights the plant-atmosphere interface as a sensitive zone for microbial community shifts under climate warming.

papers.title: Identification of ebastine and ceritinib as effective inhibitors of Fusobacterium nucleatum FtsZ.
papers.abstract: The role of microorganisms in cancer is not a new concept-bacteria, parasites, and viruses have all been implicated in cancer development. Fusobacterium nucleatum, a member of the oral microbiota, has emerged as an important cancer-associated bacterium. Unbiased global genomic analyses have demonstrated that F. nucleatum is enriched in human colorectal cancer (CRC) tissues compared with noncancerous colorectal tissues, underscoring the urgent need for specific antimicrobial agents targeting F. nucleatum for CRC prevention and treatment. In this study, structure-based virtual screening successf
papers.summary: The study used structure-based virtual screening to identify two existing drugs, ebastine and ceritinib, as effective inhibitors of FtsZ, a key bacterial cell-division protein, in the cancer-associated bacterium Fusobacterium nucleatum. Since F. nucleatum is enriched in colorectal cancer tissues, these repurposed drugs could offer a targeted antimicrobial strategy for CRC prevention or treatment.

papers.title: The protection of chronic cerebral ischemia by Hua-Feng-Dan involves the modulation of hippocampal transcriptome and gut dysbiosis.
papers.abstract: The protective effects of Hua-Feng-Dan recipes against chronic cerebral hypoperfusion-induced ischemia were examined; RNA-seq and 16 S-rRNA-seq were used to explore the molecular mechanisms. Male Sprague-Dawley rats underwent unilateral common carotid artery ligation surgery to establish chronic cerebral hypoperfusion (CCH) models. Then, the CCH rats were treated with various Hua-Feng-Dan recipes in diet for 20 days. Finally, behavioral tests were performed, followed by histopathology. Hippocampal RNA was isolated for RNA-seq and RT-qPCR analyses; Colon bacterial DNA was isolated for 16 S rRNA
papers.summary: This study investigated whether Hua-Feng-Dan, a traditional Chinese medicine formula, protects against chronic cerebral hypoperfusion (CCH) in rats. Using hippocampal RNA-seq and 16S rRNA sequencing of colon bacteria, the authors linked the treatment's protective effects on behavior and brain histopathology to changes in hippocampal gene expression and gut microbiome composition. The work suggests that Hua-Feng-Dan's neuroprotection may operate through modulation of both the hippocampal transcriptome and gut dysbiosis.

papers.title: Children at risk of vitamin A deficiency exhibit taxonomic dysbiosis and functional remodeling of the gut microbiome: a matched case-control study.
papers.abstract: Vitamin A deficiency is one of the most prevalent micronutrient deficiencies worldwide. This condition increases susceptibility to infections and due to its role in intestinal barrier integrity, it has been suggested that it could predispose to gut dysbiosis.
papers.summary: This matched case-control study examines whether children at risk of vitamin A deficiency show altered gut microbiome composition and function compared with matched controls. The authors report taxonomic dysbiosis and functional remodeling of the gut microbiome in the at-risk group, suggesting a link between vitamin A status and microbial community structure. The findings are preliminary and based on an abstract-level description, so causal direction and clinical implications remain to be established.

papers.title: Integrated optimization of experimental and computational workflows improves genome recovery in long-read gut metagenomics.
papers.abstract: Short-read metagenomic sequencing has been widely applied in microbial research due to its high quality and decreasing cost. However, short reads are inherently fragmented, which limits assembly contiguity and the recovery of complete microbial genomes. In contrast, long-read sequencing, with significantly longer read lengths, helps overcome these limitations. Achieving complete and accurate genome recovery is the core goal of metagenomics. To address this challenge, we systematically evaluated and optimized the long-read metagenomic workflow, from sample processing to computational assembly,
papers.summary: This study systematically evaluates and optimizes a long-read metagenomic workflow for gut microbiome samples, spanning sample processing through computational assembly, to improve recovery of complete microbial genomes. The integrated optimization of experimental and computational steps yields better assembly contiguity and genome recovery than standard approaches. The work provides practical guidance for labs aiming to obtain high-quality genomes from long-read metagenomics.

papers.title: Sex influences the mosquito virome in a host-specific way.
papers.abstract: Mosquitoes harbor diverse eukaryotic viruses. These viral communities, or viromes, probably influence mosquito physiology, including pathogen transmission. However, the factors shaping the virome remain largely unstudied, limiting our understanding of its role in mosquito biology. Here, we assess the influence of sex on the eukaryotic virome of mosquitoes. Ecological differences between males and females, such as female-specific blood feeding, may lead to differential viral exposure and virome structure. We investigated the influence of sex in sympatric populations of Culex quinquefasciatus an
papers.summary: This study examines how mosquito sex shapes the eukaryotic virome in sympatric populations of Culex quinquefasciatus and likely other mosquito species. The authors find that viral community composition differs between males and females in a host-species-specific manner, suggesting that ecological differences such as female blood feeding influence viral exposure and virome structure. The work highlights sex as an underappreciated factor structuring mosquito viromes, with implications for understanding vector biology and pathogen transmission.

papers.title: Diversity and evolution of the ribovirian class Stelpaviricetes.
papers.abstract: Metatranscriptome mining has dramatically expanded the known diversity of ribovirians at all taxonomic levels. We explored the class Stelpaviricetes in the phylum Pisuviricota that currently includes three orders and six recognized virus families: order Stellavirales with family Astroviridae infecting vertebrates; Patatavirales with families Potyviridae, the largest known family of plant ribovirians, and Potyliviridae; and Hypofuvirales consisting of three families of viruses associated largely with phytopathogenic fungi. Using an order-specific collection of Hidden Markov Model profiles for t
papers.summary: This study uses metatranscriptome mining with order-specific Hidden Markov Models to explore the diversity and evolution of the ribovirian class Stelpaviricetes, which includes plant, vertebrate, and fungal viruses. The work likely expands the known taxonomic diversity within this class and provides insights into the evolutionary relationships among its orders and families.

papers.title: Physiological, behavioral, and genetic factors that shape interactions in the plant growth-promoting maize rhizosphere synthetic community.
papers.abstract: Profiling microbiomes is an important way to understand the function and composition of communities in the wild, but natural microbiomes are often highly complex and often unamenable to experimentation to reveal cause-and-effect relationships. By using a small group of cultivable strains to represent those found in the wild, synthetic communities are one solution to this problem. Here we describe the maize rhizosphere synthetic community (MARSc), a genome-enabled 31-member bacterial community representative of the diversity found on the roots of maize grown in Iowa soils. This community is bui
papers.summary: The authors built MARSc, a 31-member synthetic bacterial community representing the diversity found on maize roots in Iowa soils, with genome sequences available for each strain. This resource enables controlled experiments to uncover cause-and-effect relationships among physiological, behavioral, and genetic factors that shape plant growth-promoting rhizosphere interactions.

papers.title: Exploring normality: Mapping the endometrial microbiome in healthy reproductive-aged women from Argentina.
papers.abstract: The human microbiome varies according to individual and geographic characteristics. The endometrial microbiome plays a relevant role in reproductive physiology; however, data from healthy South American populations remain scarce. This prospective observational study aimed to characterize the endometrial microbiome in healthy reproductive-aged women from Rosario, Argentina and to establish a regional baseline for future research. A total of 100 healthy women aged 22-50 years from Rosario, Argentina, were included. Endometrial samples were obtained by aspiration biopsy during the follicular phas
papers.summary: This study characterizes the endometrial microbiome in 100 healthy reproductive-aged women from Rosario, Argentina, using aspiration biopsies during the follicular phase. It provides a regional baseline for a South American population where such data were previously scarce, supporting future research on the endometrial microbiome's role in reproductive physiology.

papers.title: Monitoring single-cell metabolic phenotyping changes of Daqu microbiota during fermentation by Raman spectroscopy.
papers.abstract: Monitoring microbial community dynamics during natural food fermentation is essential for stabilizing fermentation processes and improving product flavor profiles. This study employed single-cell Raman spectroscopy to monitor the metabolic change of Daqu microbiota during fermentation. First, we developed an operational phenotypic unit (OPU)-based clustering method to process Raman spectral data of a nine-member microbial community. The clustering was validated by sorting out representative single cells from different OPUs and performing 16S/ITS region sequencing. Second, single-cell Raman spe
papers.summary: This study applies single-cell Raman spectroscopy to track metabolic changes in the microbial community of Daqu, a traditional fermentation starter, over the course of fermentation. The authors developed an operational phenotypic unit (OPU)-based clustering method for Raman spectral data and validated it by sorting representative single cells and sequencing their 16S/ITS regions. This demonstrates a label-free, single-cell approach for monitoring metabolic heterogeneity in complex fermentation microbiomes.

papers.title: Molecular mechanisms of colorectal cancer: from carcinogenesis and molecular classification to targeted therapy.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a heterogeneous disease that results from the progressive accumulation and interactions at multiple levels of genetic alterations, which lead to the transformation of normal colonic epithelium into malignant colorectal tumors. Understanding the molecular basis of CRC pathogenesis, together with the interactions between genetic alterations, epigenetic modifications, environmental and lifestyle factors, is essential for improving prevention, diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment strategies. This review aims to provide a critical reference point for understanding the temp
papers.summary: This review synthesizes the molecular mechanisms underlying colorectal cancer, covering the stepwise genetic and epigenetic alterations that drive normal colonic epithelium toward malignancy. It discusses how these molecular changes inform tumor classification and the development of targeted therapies, emphasizing interactions between genetic, epigenetic, and environmental factors. The work serves as a consolidated reference for understanding CRC pathogenesis and translating molecular insights into clinical strategies.

papers.title: Shotgun metagenomic characterization of human adenovirus F40 and a non-cpe Clostridium perfringens strain in pediatric prolonged diarrhea: a genome-resolved case study.
papers.abstract: Viral and bacterial pathogens may be concurrently detected in pediatric gastroenteritis, yet such findings are often missed by routine diagnostic methods. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing enables comprehensive detection and genomic characterization of microorganisms present in clinical specimens, including pathogens that may not be recovered by conventional testing.
papers.summary: This case study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize human adenovirus F40 and a non-cpe Clostridium perfringens strain in a pediatric patient with prolonged diarrhea. The work demonstrates that metagenomics can detect and genomically resolve co-infecting pathogens missed by routine diagnostics, though as a single case it provides limited generalizable insight.

papers.title: Genome-resolved taxonomy, global distribution, and EPS potential of Zoogloea, the canonical floc-former in wastewater treatment systems.
papers.abstract: The bacterial genus Zoogloea is the fourth most abundant genus in wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) globally, where it plays key roles in floc formation and nutrient removal but can also contribute to viscous bulking when highly abundant. The taxonomic assignment of Zoogloea has historically been inconsistent, as several taxa were classified based on phenotypic characteristics and later reassigned to other families or orders. This has obscured both the identity and distribution of Zoogloea and hindered interpretation of its floc-forming mechanisms, which have been attributed to polysaccharid
papers.summary: This study uses genome-resolved taxonomy to clarify the classification of Zoogloea, the fourth most abundant bacterial genus in wastewater treatment plants worldwide, resolving historical inconsistencies in its taxonomic assignment. It maps the genus's global distribution and assesses its potential for producing extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) that drive floc formation and nutrient removal, while also noting risks of viscous bulking at high abundance.

papers.title: Global Carriage of Antimicrobial Resistance Genes and Virulence Factors Among Physicians in Cirrhosis Care.
papers.abstract: Cirrhosis patients are at high risk for drug-resistant infections, which may be transmitted between patients and healthcare providers. In this study, we used shotgun metagenomics to characterize the fecal microbiome of physicians in cirrhosis care (n = 55) across 9 countries. Our results indicate physicians from low- or middle-income countries carry greater antimicrobial resistance gene (ARG) diversity corresponding to increased taxonomic richness. Physicians carried a low prevalence of clinically relevant ARGs or virulence factors (VFs), regardless of country of practice or patient exposure.
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomics to profile the fecal microbiomes of 55 physicians caring for cirrhosis patients across 9 countries, examining carriage of antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) and virulence factors (VFs). Physicians in low- and middle-income countries showed greater ARG diversity, which tracked with increased taxonomic richness, but overall carriage of clinically relevant ARGs and VFs was low regardless of country or patient exposure. The findings suggest that healthcare providers in cirrhosis care carry a modest resistance burden, with geographic income level shaping gut resistome diversity more than occupational exposure.

papers.title: Importance of rumen ciliated protozoa and current research techniques for their analysis.
papers.abstract: Rumen protozoa are an integral component of the ruminant foregut microbiome, with a profound influence on feed digestion, microbial ecosystem dynamics and enteric methane emissions. Although they represent only a small proportion of species richness, protozoa contribute significantly to microbial biomass and functions in fibre degradation, volatile fatty acid production, microbial protein turnover, pH modulation and hydrogen-mediated methanogenesis. In addition to highlighting their importance to rumen function, this review summarizes classical and contemporary methodologies for enumerating, i
papers.summary: This review highlights the importance of rumen ciliated protozoa in the ruminant foregut microbiome, noting their outsized contributions to fibre digestion, volatile fatty acid production, microbial protein turnover, pH modulation, and hydrogen-mediated methane emissions despite low species richness. It also surveys classical and modern methods for enumerating and analysing these protozoa, providing a methodological reference for researchers studying rumen ecology.

papers.title: Infective endocarditis due to a novel Gemella species revealed by metagenomic sequencing.
papers.abstract: Gemella species are rare causes of infective endocarditis, and accurate species identification can be challenging with routine diagnostic methods. We report infective endocarditis caused by a novel Gemella species, highlighting the diagnostic value of sequencing-based approaches for bacteria not registered in public databases and the risk of misclassification when novel species are not represented in reference databases.
papers.summary: This case report describes a patient with infective endocarditis caused by a previously unknown Gemella species, identified through metagenomic sequencing after routine diagnostic methods failed to provide accurate species-level identification. The case highlights how sequencing-based approaches can detect novel pathogens absent from public reference databases, while also illustrating the risk of misclassification when such species are not represented.

papers.title: Benchmarking nanopore-based strategies for antimicrobial resistance prediction.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) presents a pressing need to ensure that the right antimicrobials are used to target the right microbes at the right time. Ideally, the appropriate antimicrobial is selected after patient samples have been cultured and assessed with antimicrobial sensitivity testing (AST). However, the time needed for culture-based diagnosis leads to immediate empirical treatment, often with broad-spectrum and/or high-tier antimicrobials. Direct nanopore metagenomic whole-genome sequencing to identify pathogens and predict their AMR is a rapid and patient-side alternative. A limit
papers.summary: This study benchmarks different nanopore sequencing strategies for predicting antimicrobial resistance directly from patient samples, aiming to bypass the time-consuming culture-based diagnosis. The authors compare approaches for rapid, patient-side metagenomic whole-genome sequencing to identify pathogens and their resistance profiles, though the abstract is truncated and specific results are not fully detailed.

papers.title: Seasonal and Environmental Influences on Microbial Community Dynamics in the Dunk River Watershed, Prince Edward Island, Canada.
papers.abstract: Riverine ecosystems are crucial biogeochemical hubs, with their microbial communities playing a key role in nutrient cycling and overall ecosystem health. This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize the seasonal and environmental drivers of taxonomic and functional microbial community structure (read depth between 1.91 and 30.44 bp) in four tributaries of the Dunk River watershed in Prince Edward Island (PEI), a landscape shaped by intensive agriculture and groundwater-dominated streamflow, where the seasonal and land-use impacts on the river's microbiome remain understudied
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize how seasonal and environmental factors shape microbial community taxonomy and function across four tributaries of the Dunk River watershed in Prince Edward Island, a landscape dominated by intensive agriculture and groundwater-fed streams. The work identifies seasonal and land-use drivers of riverine microbiome structure in an understudied agricultural watershed.

papers.title: Senimuribacter muris sp. nov., a butyrate-producing bacterium isolated from mouse feces, and reclassification of members of the family Eubacteriaceae into the family Anaerovoracaceae.
papers.abstract: Two strictly anaerobic, Gram-stain-positive, non-motile, and rod-shaped bacterial strains, designated rT4E-8T and mB4P-1, were isolated from the feces of specific-pathogen-free Mus musculus (C57BL/6J). Both strains were catalase- and oxidase-negative and produced butyrate as a major fermentation product, with optimal growth at 37 °C and pH 7. The two strains shared 100% pairwise 16S rRNA gene sequence similarity and showed high similarity to Senimuribacter intestinalis DSM 106208T (95.1-95.3%). Genome sizes of strains rT4E-8T and mB4P-1 were 2.9 Mbp and 2.8 Mbp, with genomic DNA G+C contents o
papers.summary: The authors isolated two strictly anaerobic, butyrate-producing bacterial strains from mouse feces and characterized them as a new species, Senimuribacter muris. Based on 16S rRNA gene similarity and genomic data, they also propose reclassifying members of the family Eubacteriaceae into the family Anaerovoracaceae. This work expands the known diversity of gut-associated bacteria and revises the taxonomy of a relevant bacterial group.

papers.title: Jiawei Duhuo Jisheng Mixture Alleviates Knee Osteoarthritis via Inhibition of TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB Signaling and Is Associated With Gut Microbiota Alterations.
papers.abstract: To evaluate the chondroprotective effects of Jiawei Duhuo Jisheng Mixture (JDJM) in KOA and to determine whether JDJM modulates the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB axis and is associated with gut microbiota alterations.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether a traditional Chinese herbal formula, Jiawei Duhuo Jisheng Mixture, protects cartilage in knee osteoarthritis by blocking the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB inflammatory pathway and by shifting the gut microbiome. The work links herbal treatment efficacy to both a specific inflammatory signaling axis and microbiota changes, suggesting a gut-joint axis mechanism.

papers.title: Modification of kefir grain by yeast substitution and long-term stability of the microbiota of kefir grain.
papers.abstract: The yeast microbiota of kefir grains is highly diverse. Whereas one type of kefir grain contains lactose-fermenting yeast, a second type may not. The presence of lactose-fermenting yeast influences the flavor and shelf life of kefir by promoting alcoholic fermentation and the attendant formation of carbon dioxide gas. To suppress gas production, we developed a method in 1994 to modify the yeast microbiota of kefir grain. The traditional kefir grain (TCHR grain) contains a lactose-fermenting yeast (Kluyveromyces marxianus) and 2 non-lactose-fermenting yeasts (Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Kazach
papers.summary: The authors describe a 1994 method for modifying the yeast microbiota of kefir grains by substituting lactose-fermenting yeast with non-lactose-fermenting strains to suppress gas production, and they report on the long-term stability of the resulting grain microbiota. The traditional grain contained Kluyveromyces marxianus plus Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Kazachstania species, and the modified grain's microbial community remained stable over extended cultivation.

papers.title: Probiotics and diarrhoea morbidity among infants in Tanzania: secondary analysis of a randomised clinical trial.
papers.abstract: Diarrhoea causes annually more than 444 000 deaths in children globally, the majority in infants in low-income countries. The gut microbiota is a key determinant in resilience against enteric infections. We evaluated the effects of Bifidobacterium-based probiotic supplementation on diarrhoea morbidity among infants in Tanzania and explored associations between the gut microbiota composition at 6 weeks of age and later diarrhoeal risk.
papers.summary: This secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial in Tanzania examined whether Bifidobacterium-based probiotic supplementation reduces diarrhoea morbidity in infants, and whether gut microbiota composition at 6 weeks of age predicts later diarrhoeal risk. The study explores links between early-life microbiome and resilience to enteric infections in a low-income setting.

papers.title: CAnDi: a global catalogue of anaerobic digestion microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Methanogenic environments harbour complex prokaryotic consortia that drive the anaerobic conversion of organic matter into methane and carbon dioxide. Beyond being key to the global carbon cycle, such processes have been steered into powerful biotechnologies for energy production in bioreactors. Decoding the functional and taxonomic landscape of these communities requires comprehensive surveys, including bacteriophages and plasmids, which, however, remain vastly underrepresented in current databases. Here, we present the microbial Catalogue of Anaerobic Digestion (CAnDi), a database comprising
papers.summary: CAnDi is a new global database that catalogues the microbiomes involved in anaerobic digestion, including bacteria, archaea, bacteriophages, and plasmids. It addresses the underrepresentation of these communities and their mobile genetic elements in existing databases, providing a comprehensive resource for studying methane-producing consortia in both natural and engineered environments.

papers.title: Influence of Gliricidia sepium living support on rhizosphere bacterial recruitment and fruit metabolomics in black pepper (Piper nigrum).
papers.abstract: The ability of the rhizosphere to recruit beneficial microorganisms is central to the sustainable management of crops. Here, we investigated, through shotgun metagenomic sequencing and mass spectrometry techniques, the microbial composition, antimicrobial resistance (AMRs), and metabolomic profiles of Piper nigrum cultivated under two support systems: living Gliricidia sepium support (SL/RL) and dead wooden support (SD/RD). Bulk and rhizosphere soils were sequenced to assess taxonomic structure and ARGs, with emphasis on Actinobacteria due to their relevance in antibiotic production. Actinobac
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomics and mass spectrometry to compare the rhizosphere microbiome and fruit metabolome of black pepper grown on living Gliricidia sepium supports versus dead wooden supports. It found that living supports influence bacterial recruitment—particularly Actinobacteria—and antimicrobial resistance gene profiles in the rhizosphere, with corresponding differences in fruit metabolites. The work links agricultural support systems to belowground microbial ecology and crop chemistry.

papers.title: Assembly of minimally fragmented metagenomic pangenome graphs.
papers.abstract: Pangenome variation graphs are a powerful tool for representing genetic diversity within and across populations. For comparative and evolutionary genomic analyses leveraging these graph-based structures, it is important that graph topology reflects the underlying phylogenetic and genetic similarities of the genomes embedded within the graph. However, in metagenomic settings these approaches often produce highly fragmented multi-component graphs, hindering comparisons of genomes embedded across different components. This challenge is particularly pronounced for hypervariable viral families like
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint addresses the problem of fragmented pangenome variation graphs in metagenomic settings, where highly variable viral families produce multi-component graphs that hinder comparative and evolutionary analyses. The authors propose an assembly approach aimed at producing minimally fragmented graphs so that graph topology better reflects the underlying phylogenetic and genetic relationships among embedded genomes.

papers.title: Network perturbation of lactate metabolism identifies an aggressive hepatocellular carcinoma subtype with distinct immune and microbial features.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) exhibits significant heterogeneity, and the reprogramming of lactate metabolism (LM) plays a crucial role in tumor progression and immune evasion. Classification based on perturbations in the gene interaction network related to LM may reveal new molecular subtypes. This study aimed to construct an LM interaction perturbation-based classification of HCC and to characterize the clinical, immune, and intratumoral microbial features of the identified subtypes.
papers.summary: This study classifies hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) into molecular subtypes by analyzing perturbations in the gene interaction network related to lactate metabolism. It identifies an aggressive HCC subtype with distinct immune and intratumoral microbial features, suggesting that network-based classification can reveal clinically relevant heterogeneity beyond standard expression profiling.

papers.title: An integrated in vitro gastrointestinal digestion and fermentation model as a complementary tool for evaluating feed ingredients in young broilers: a case study with peas.
papers.abstract: The search for sustainable protein sources in broiler nutrition has increased interest in locally produced ingredients such as peas. However, nutritional evaluation of alternative feed ingredients relies on costly and ethically constrained animal trials, while standardized in vitro models representing the complete gastrointestinal tract of young broilers are lacking. These models should reflect their lower digestive capacity and less complex caecal microbiota. This study developed an innovative in vitro model simulating the complete gastrointestinal tract of young broilers and used peas as a c
papers.summary: This study developed an integrated in vitro model that simulates the complete gastrointestinal tract of young broilers, including digestion and caecal fermentation, to evaluate feed ingredients without animal trials. Using peas as a case study, the model captures the lower digestive capacity and simpler caecal microbiota characteristic of young birds, offering a cost-effective and ethically preferable alternative to in vivo nutritional evaluation.

papers.title: Microbial community structure and functional gene profiles of drinking water treatment plant sludge in South Africa: An exploratory pilot study.
papers.abstract: Microbial characterization of drinking water treatment plant (DWTP) sludge helps inform sludge management strategies and supports the development of disposal policies and procedures. In South Africa, the microbial composition of DWTP sludge remains poorly documented. This study characterised the microbial communities and functional gene profiles in sludge samples collected from three DWTPs in Gauteng, Limpopo, and Mpumalanga. A shotgun metagenomic approach was employed to provide a broad assessment of microbial taxa and functional gene categories, while physicochemical analyses were conducted
papers.summary: This pilot study used shotgun metagenomics to characterize the microbial communities and functional gene profiles in drinking water treatment plant sludge from three South African provinces, alongside physicochemical analyses. It provides some of the first baseline microbial data for DWTP sludge in South Africa, which could inform sludge management and disposal policies. The work is exploratory and limited in scope, but fills a documented data gap for the region.

papers.title: Effects of a multistrain probiotic formulation on immune response and microbiome modulation following influenza vaccination in adults: a randomised, triple-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Seasonal influenza remains a major global health burden, despite widespread vaccination. Vaccine responsiveness varies considerably between individuals and is increasingly recognised to be influenced by host factors, including the gut microbiome. Probiotics have been proposed as a strategy to modulate microbiome-immune interactions, although their effects on vaccine responses and the underlying microbial mechanisms remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This triple-blind, placebo-controlled trial tested whether a multistrain probiotic formulation could improve immune responses to influenza vaccination in adults by modulating the gut microbiome. The study examines links between probiotic supplementation, microbiome composition, and vaccine-induced immunity, addressing how host-microbiome interactions shape vaccine responsiveness. It provides randomized controlled evidence on whether probiotics can serve as an adjuvant strategy for improving vaccine efficacy.

papers.title: Deciphering the gut-lung axis in non-small cell lung cancer: from immune microenvironment crosstalk to clinical translation.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) targeting the PD-1/PD-L1 axis have established a new standard of care for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); however, clinical efficacy is frequently limited by primary resistance, acquired (secondary) resistance, and immune-related adverse events. The heterogeneity of the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) is a critical determinant of therapeutic response, a state effectively regulated by the gut microbiota via the gut-lung axis. This review systematically examines the mechanistic crosstalk between intestinal commensals and the pulmonary TIME. We first d
papers.summary: This review examines how gut microbiota influence the tumor immune microenvironment in non-small cell lung cancer through the gut-lung axis, affecting responses to PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitors. It synthesizes mechanisms of microbial-immune crosstalk and discusses implications for overcoming resistance and immune-related adverse events, with a focus on clinical translation.

papers.title: The interaction mechanisms between sarcopenia and gut microbiota based on the gut-muscle axis.
papers.abstract: Advances in high-throughput sequencing and metagenomics have improved our understanding of the gut microbiota and its associations with disease development and treatment response. The relationship between the gut microbiota and sarcopenia has attracted increasing attention in recent years. In this narrative review, we searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, CNKI, Wanfang Data, and VIP through April 2,026 and synthesized 29 human studies included in the narrative analysis together with relevant preclinical evidence. We summarize reported alterations in microbial diversity, taxonomic compositio
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes 29 human studies plus preclinical evidence on how gut microbiota composition and diversity relate to sarcopenia (age-related muscle loss) via the gut-muscle axis. It catalogs reported microbial alterations and discusses proposed interaction mechanisms linking the microbiome to muscle health. As a review, it consolidates existing evidence rather than presenting new data.

papers.title: Metagenomic characterization of gut microbiota in patients with Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction.
papers.abstract: Patients with Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction (DGBI) experience recurrent gastrointestinal symptoms without identifiable organic abnormalities. While earlier studies focused on neural and hormonal regulation, recent evidence suggests that gut microbiota dysbiosis and altered microbial metabolism may play key roles in DGBI.
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomic sequencing to characterize the gut microbiota composition and functional potential in patients with Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction (DGBI), a group of chronic gastrointestinal conditions without identifiable organic cause. The authors compare microbial profiles between DGBI patients and controls to identify dysbiosis patterns and altered metabolic pathways that may contribute to symptom generation. The work adds to growing evidence linking gut microbial ecology to gut-brain axis dysfunction.

papers.title: Metagenomic analysis of tomato rhizosphere microbiomes detects Ralstonia phage sequences in Kenyan agricultural soils.
papers.abstract: Bacterial wilt caused by Ralstonia solanacearum species complex is a major constraint in tomato production in Kenya, resulting in yield losses of up to 100% in heavily infested fields. This study used high-throughput shotgun metagenomic sequencing approach to characterize the rhizosphere microbiomes of tomato plants in three of the major production areas in Kenya (Kirinyaga, Kiambu, and Laikipia counties) focusing on detecting Ralstonia phage sequences. Soil samples were collected from the rhizosphere of bacterial wilt-infected tomato plants, and microbial DNA was extracted using a modified ph
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize tomato rhizosphere microbiomes from three major tomato-growing regions in Kenya, with a focus on detecting Ralstonia phage sequences in soils where bacterial wilt is a severe problem. The work demonstrates that phage sequences associated with the Ralstonia solanacearum species complex can be detected in agricultural soils, suggesting a potential avenue for biocontrol of this devastating pathogen.

papers.title: Association of in utero and postnatal drought exposure with health and anthropometric outcomes in children under-five: A systematic review.
papers.abstract: Drought poses multiple health risks that may affect children both prenatally and during early childhood, yet the evidence remains fragmented. We conducted a systematic review to synthesize evidence from observational studies assessing the association between drought exposure during pregnancy and the first five years of life and child health and anthropometric outcomes. The review protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD4202338273). We searched 18 databases and complemented the search with grey literature and manual reference screening. Two independent reviewers screened studies and assessed ri
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes observational evidence on how drought exposure during pregnancy and early childhood affects health and growth outcomes in children under five. The authors searched 18 databases plus grey literature, finding fragmented but suggestive evidence linking drought exposure to adverse child health and anthropometric outcomes. The review highlights the need for more consistent research on climate-related exposures in early life.

papers.title: Microbiome variation across the intestinal dysbiosis landscape is linked to inflammation and transit time.
papers.abstract: Intestinal dysbiosis, an imbalance in gut microbial composition and host-microbiome interaction, has been linked to various conditions and disorders. Although characterised by multiple features, such as reduced microbial diversity and bacterial load, as well as an underrepresentation of beneficial microorganisms and an overrepresentation of pathobionts, an exact definition remains elusive. Whether all dysbiotic individuals share similar microbial composition and host properties is currently unclear.
papers.summary: This study maps microbiome variation across the spectrum of intestinal dysbiosis, showing that dysbiotic states are not uniform but vary substantially in microbial composition. The variation is linked to host inflammation and gut transit time, suggesting these factors help explain different dysbiosis subtypes. The work argues against a single definition of dysbiosis and toward context-dependent characterization.

papers.title: Metadoon: A user-friendly GUI for amplicon analysis.
papers.abstract: The analysis of microbial communities through 16S rRNA gene sequencing plays a central role in microbial ecology and host-associated microbiome research. However, the complexity of existing bioinformatic tools often limits their use by researchers without computational expertise. We present Metadoon, a graphical pipeline designed to automate the analysis of amplicon sequencing data targeting the V3-V4 regions of the 16S rRNA gene. Developed in Python and integrating VSEARCH and R, Metadoon performs quality filtering, OTU clustering, taxonomic classification, and diversity analysis through an i
papers.summary: Metadoon is a Python-based graphical user interface that automates 16S rRNA V3-V4 amplicon analysis by integrating VSEARCH and R for quality filtering, OTU clustering, taxonomic classification, and diversity analysis. It aims to make microbiome bioinformatics accessible to researchers without computational expertise by replacing command-line workflows with a point-and-click pipeline.

papers.title: Current status and trends of gut microbiota in the study of cognitive impairment in the elderly.
papers.abstract: Cognitive impairment in older persons has become a major public health concern as the world's population ages more quickly. A reduction in thinking, learning, and memory skills that affects a person's day-to-day activities or social functioning is referred to as cognitive impairment. The connection between gut microbiota and cognitive decline has attracted a lot of interest lately. However, this rapidly expanding interdisciplinary field presents an increasingly complex knowledge structure, with existing evidence being highly fragmented and subject to significant methodological and sample size
papers.summary: This review examines the current state of research linking gut microbiota to cognitive impairment in older adults, noting that the field is expanding rapidly but remains fragmented. The authors highlight that existing evidence is limited by methodological inconsistencies and small sample sizes, and they outline trends and gaps in this interdisciplinary area.

papers.title: Plant-Derived Exosome-Like Nanoparticles: Biological Functions, Therapeutic Applications, and Translational Challenges.
papers.abstract: Plant-derived herbal medicines remain important sources of bioactive compounds, but their clinical application is often hindered by poor bioavailability and variable pharmacokinetic profiles. Recent studies have identified plant-derived exosome-like nanoparticles (PELNs) as naturally occurring bioactive nanoparticle preparations containing proteins, lipids, small RNAs, and secondary metabolites. This review examines advances in PELN isolation, biological properties, and their therapeutic applications, with particular emphasis on immune regulation, gut-microbiota modulation, and bone homeostasi
papers.summary: This review surveys plant-derived exosome-like nanoparticles (PELNs), naturally occurring vesicles containing proteins, lipids, small RNAs, and secondary metabolites that may improve the bioavailability of herbal bioactives. It covers isolation methods, biological properties, and therapeutic applications, focusing on immune regulation, gut-microbiota modulation, and bone homeostasis, while discussing translational challenges.

papers.title: Integrated gut microbiome and fecal metabolome profiling identifies taurine-associated microbial dysbiosis across the Alzheimer's disease clinical spectrum.
papers.abstract: Gut microbiome alterations have been associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD), but how microbial composition, fecal metabolites, and cognitive function relate across the cognitive impairment spectrum-from subjective cognitive decline (SCD) through mild cognitive impairment (MCI) to AD-remains unclear. We integrated microbiome and metabolome profiles across this clinical spectrum.
papers.summary: This study integrates gut microbiome and fecal metabolome profiling across the Alzheimer's disease clinical spectrum, from subjective cognitive decline through mild cognitive impairment to AD. The authors identify taurine-associated microbial dysbiosis that tracks with cognitive impairment severity, suggesting a link between microbial metabolism and AD progression.

papers.title: Microbiome-guided rhizosphere engineering for sustainable remediation of agricultural soil contaminants.
papers.abstract: Agricultural soils increasingly carry mixtures of pesticide residues, heavy metals, petroleum hydrocarbons and microplastics, and conventional phytoremediation is too slow and too contaminant-specific to address them. Rhizosphere engineering, the deliberate manipulation of root-associated microbial communities, is widely proposed as the alternative, but the literature reports laboratory, pot and field results in a single register, so a reader cannot easily tell which approaches are deployable. This mini-review stratifies that evidence rather than surveying it. Every approach examined is assign
papers.summary: This mini-review argues that rhizosphere engineering—deliberately manipulating root-associated microbes—could help clean up agricultural soils contaminated with mixtures of pesticides, heavy metals, hydrocarbons, and microplastics, where conventional phytoremediation is too slow and narrow. Its main contribution is methodological: it stratifies the evidence from lab, pot, and field studies so readers can distinguish approaches that are actually deployable from those that only work under controlled conditions.

papers.title: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) mediated gut breast crosstalk in breast cancer: integrative network analysis of molecular signaling, immune infiltration and prognostic biomarkers.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer is a heterogeneous malignancy in which metabolic dysregulation, immune remodelling, and complex host microbiota interactions contribute to disease progression and therapeutic response. Emerging evidence suggests that gut microbiota-derived short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), including acetate, propionate, and butyrate, may act as important molecular mediators linking the gut microbiome to systemic immune and tumor-associated signalling. However, the molecular networks through which SCFA-mediated signalling may influence breast cancer progression and the tumor immune microenvironment
papers.summary: This integrative network analysis explores how gut microbiome-derived short-chain fatty acids (acetate, propionate, butyrate) may influence breast cancer through molecular signaling and immune remodeling. The authors construct signaling networks linking SCFA-mediated pathways to tumor immune microenvironment features and identify candidate prognostic biomarkers. The work is largely computational and hypothesis-generating, connecting microbiome metabolism to breast cancer biology.

papers.title: Impact of rumen microbiome sample handling and extraction procedures on downstream long-read sequencing.
papers.abstract: The rumen microbiome is a complex microbial ecosystem central to ruminant nutrition and productivity. Long-read sequencing technologies, such as Oxford Nanopore, have greatly improved resolution of strain-level diversity and enabled assembly of near-complete genomes, but these benefits depend on the integrity and purity of input DNA, which can be affected by sample preservation and extraction methods. This study evaluated multiple DNA extraction protocols to best maximize high-molecular-weight DNA recovery for long-read sequencing and whether flash freezing or freezing and thawing samples bias
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study tested different DNA extraction protocols and sample preservation methods (flash freezing vs. freeze-thaw) to determine how they affect high-molecular-weight DNA recovery and downstream Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing of the rumen microbiome. The authors identify extraction and handling procedures that maximize DNA integrity and minimize bias, providing practical guidance for strain-level and near-complete genome assembly from complex microbial communities.

papers.title: Genetic diversity of bacterial endophytes associated with Crotalaria (Rattlepods).
papers.abstract: Crotalaria is a diverse legume genus valued for its ecological and agronomic roles. However, its associated endophytic microbiome remains minimally characterized. This study examined the genetic diversity and community structure of bacterial endophytes inhabiting domesticated and wild Crotalaria species. Twenty-nine healthy Crotalaria plant samples were analyzed using the culture-independent 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing approach. Genomic DNA was extracted using the Phenol-Chloroform method from both domesticated and wild samples. Sequencing of 16S ribosomal RNA gene was performed using Il
papers.summary: This study used 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing to characterize the bacterial endophyte communities living inside domesticated and wild Crotalaria (rattlepod) legumes, a genus whose endophytic microbiome had been poorly described. The authors compared community diversity and structure across 29 healthy plant samples, providing a baseline survey of the bacteria associated with this ecologically and agronomically important legume.

papers.title: Microbiota-mediated blocking of plasmodium falciparum sporozoites in Anopheles: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: The development of Plasmodium falciparum sporozoites in the mosquito, Anopheles, is essential for malaria transmission. Despite the unsurprising fact that the mosquito microbiota has become a major factor in the modulation of the competence of mosquitoes, the specific types of microbial taxa and mechanisms affecting the development of the sporozoite are not well synthesized. This systematic review brings together and critically evaluates the available evidence to understand the role of microbiota in the development of P. falciparum sporozoites in Anopheles mosquitoes with a specific focus on t
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes evidence on how the mosquito microbiota influences the development of Plasmodium falciparum sporozoites in Anopheles mosquitoes, a critical step for malaria transmission. It compiles the microbial taxa and mechanisms reported to block or modulate sporozoite development, highlighting the potential of microbiota-based strategies to reduce transmission. The review critically evaluates the available evidence and identifies gaps for future research.

papers.title: Changes in the Gut Microbiota Composition and Metabolic Pathways in Six-Week-Old HIV Exposed Breastfed Infants Receiving Antiretroviral Prophylaxis.
papers.abstract: Understanding the association of HIV exposure, antiretroviral therapy (ART) prophylaxis and human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) on the gut microbiota of breastfed infants is crucial for developing strategies to promote infant health. Our study explored gut microbiota diversity and development in breastfed infants, analysing the influence of nevirapine (NVP) in HIV Exposed infants and HMOs in HIV Unexposed infants.
papers.summary: This study examined how HIV exposure and antiretroviral prophylaxis (nevirapine) affect gut microbiota composition and metabolic pathways in six-week-old breastfed infants, comparing HIV-exposed infants receiving NVP with HIV-unexposed infants. The findings suggest that both HIV exposure/ART prophylaxis and human milk oligosaccharides influence microbiota diversity and development, with potential implications for infant health strategies.

papers.title: Edible insect-based feed ingredients as modulators of gastrointestinal physiology in monogastric livestock and aquaculture species.
papers.abstract: Edible insects have emerged as promising sustainable feed ingredients capable of supporting both animal production and gastrointestinal health. Beyond their nutritional value, insect-derived meals contain bioactive compounds-including chitin, antimicrobial peptides, medium-chain fatty acids, micronutrients, and antioxidant molecules-that may modulate gut microbiota-host interactions in farmed monogastric animal species. This review critically examines current evidence on the mechanisms through which insect-based diets influence gastrointestinal physiology in livestock and aquaculture species.
papers.summary: This review examines how edible insect-based feed ingredients can influence gastrointestinal physiology in monogastric livestock and aquaculture species. It highlights that beyond nutrition, insect meals contain bioactive compounds such as chitin, antimicrobial peptides, and medium-chain fatty acids that may modulate gut microbiota-host interactions. The authors critically assess current evidence for these mechanisms and their potential to support both animal production and gut health.

papers.title: Clear aligner interface properties, oral microbial ecology, and strategies for biofilm control and caries-risk mitigation: a scoping review.
papers.abstract: Clear aligners create an aligner-tooth interface that may retain saliva, microorganisms, and dietary substrates. Evidence linking interface properties, oral microecological responses, and preventive interventions remains fragmented.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This scoping review examines how the physical and chemical properties of clear aligner surfaces and the aligner-tooth interface influence oral microbial ecology, including biofilm formation and caries risk. It also surveys preventive strategies for biofilm control and caries-risk mitigation in aligner wearers, highlighting that current evidence is fragmented and that standardized approaches are needed.

papers.title: Characterization of lower-airway microbial communities in pulmonary tuberculosis by BALF metagenomic sequencing.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) is an infectious disease caused by the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC). This study aimed to characterize the lower-airway microbiome in patients with PTB and compare it with that of patients without PTB (Non-PTB) undergoing bronchoscopy for pulmonary disease, in order to describe differences in microbial composition between the two groups and improve our understanding of pulmonary microbial ecology in tuberculosis.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study used metagenomic sequencing of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) to characterize the lower-airway microbial communities of patients with pulmonary tuberculosis compared to patients without PTB undergoing bronchoscopy. It describes differences in microbial composition between the two groups, aiming to improve understanding of pulmonary microbial ecology in tuberculosis. The work provides a descriptive baseline of the lower-airway microbiome in PTB.

papers.title: Decoding pyroptosis at single-cell resolution: heterogeneity, microenvironment remodeling and potential translational insights.
papers.abstract: Pyroptosis, a pro-inflammatory programmed cell death mediated by inflammatory caspases and Gasdermin (GSDM) family proteins, exerts dual roles in host defense and pathological damage. Traditional bulk RNA sequencing (bulk RNA-seq) is limited in capturing single-cell heterogeneity and dissecting intercellular communication, impeding in-depth mechanistic exploration of pyroptosis. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has emerged as a powerful tool to address these limitations, enabling high-throughput profiling of single-cell transcriptomes and precise characterization of gene expression heter
papers.summary: This review argues that single-cell RNA sequencing offers a powerful way to study pyroptosis, an inflammatory form of programmed cell death, by capturing cell-to-cell heterogeneity and intercellular communication that bulk RNA-seq misses. It surveys how scRNA-seq reveals pyroptosis-related heterogeneity, remodeling of the tumor or tissue microenvironment, and potential translational applications. The paper is a synthesis of existing literature rather than new data.

papers.title: Harnessing metatranscriptomics to unveil the metabolic landscape of microbiota in traditional fermented foods.
papers.abstract: Traditional fermented foods are widely consumed and valued for their distinctive sensory properties and potential health benefits. These foods contain complex microbiota whose interactions and metabolic activities shape biochemical transformations relevant to product quality, safety, and functionality. Metatranscriptomics provides a culture-independent means of profiling community RNA and examining changes in microbial gene expression during fermentation. However, most fermented-food microbiome studies continue to infer function from community composition or genomic potential rather than from
papers.summary: This review argues that metatranscriptomics—sequencing community RNA rather than DNA—can reveal which microbial genes are actually active during traditional fermented food production, going beyond the functional inferences typically drawn from community composition or genomic potential alone. It surveys how this approach can map the metabolic landscape of fermenting microbiota and connect gene expression to product quality, safety, and functionality.
